learn.hook: Diwali is coming! Each garland has 10 marigolds. Count the flowers in tens.
points: Each garland has 10 flowers.
Count garlands in tens: 3 garlands have 30 flowers.
A table helps: garlands in one row, flowers in the next.
To find the total for two children, add their flowers.

example.q: Meena makes 3 garlands and Raju makes 4. How many flowers did they use?

learn.reallife: Flower sellers near temples string marigolds into garlands.

quiz.q: Each garland has 10 flowers. How many flowers are in 6 garlands?
Asha uses 40 flowers to make garlands of 10. How many garlands did she make?
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of flowers instead of garlands

quiz.q: Fill the table. Garlands: 1, 2, 3, 4. Flowers: 10, 20, 30, ___.
Tina makes 2 garlands. Dev makes 5 garlands. How many flowers did they use in all?
Gopal used 50 flowers and Sita used 30 flowers. How many flowers altogether?
Zara has made 9 garlands. She needs 10 garlands. How many more flowers does she need?
quiz.explain: She needs 1 more garland, and 1 garland has 10 flowers.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of garlands, not flowers

teach.ask: Gappu: Each garland has 10 flowers. How many flowers are in 4 garlands?
teach.nudge: How many flowers in one garland? So count in what?

topics.title: Adding on a ginladi and a number line

learn.hook: Slide beads, hop on lines. Adding can be a game!
points: On a ginladi, move beads for the first number, then move more beads for the second number.
Count all the moved beads to get the total.
On a number line, start at the first number and jump forward.
Jump in tens first, then in ones: 34 + 23 goes 34, 44, 54, then 55, 56, 57.
learn.reallife: Children add their hops while playing hopscotch.

games.title: Jumps for 34 + 23
games.prompt: Put the landing numbers in order for 34 + 23

quiz.q: On a ginladi, Rani moves 20 beads, then 15 more. How many beads did she move?
Start at 26 on a number line. Jump 10 forward. Where do you land?
Om adds 34 + 23 on a number line. He jumps 10, 10 and then 3 ones from 34. Where does he land?
A number line shows jumps from 18 to 28 and then to 30. Which addition is it?
quiz.explain: 18 to 28 is a jump of 10. 28 to 30 is a jump of 2. 10 + 2 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one of the jumps

quiz.q: Use jumps to find 45 + 21.
quiz.mistake: Jumps one ten too few or too many

quiz.q: Kiran finds 52 + 4 by moving 4 more beads after 52. What is the total?

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I add 34 + 23 on a number line?
teach.praise: Yes! Start at 34, jump 2 tens and then 3 ones to reach 57.
teach.nudge: Where do I start? What jumps do I make?

topics.title: Adding with blocks and in columns

learn.hook: Rods are tens and cubes are ones. Put them together to add!
points: A tens rod has 10 blocks. A small cube is 1.
Put rods with rods and cubes with cubes, then count.
Write numbers in columns: tens under tens, ones under ones.
Add the ones column first, then the tens. If the ones make 10 or more, carry 1 ten.
learn.reallife: Shopkeepers write bills in columns to add them up.

quiz.q: Sonu has 3 rods and 4 cubes. Jaya has 2 rods and 5 cubes. How many blocks in all?
quiz.explain: Rods: 3 + 2 = 5 tens. Cubes: 4 + 5 = 9 ones. That is 59.

quiz.q: In column addition, which column do we add first?
quiz.explain: We add the ones first, so we can carry a new ten if needed.

quiz.q: Add in columns: 47 + 25
In 38 + 46, the ones make 8 + 6 = 14. What do we write in the ones place?
quiz.explain: 14 is 1 ten and 4 ones. Write 4 and carry the 1 ten.
quiz.mistake: Writes the whole 14 in the ones place

quiz.q: Add in columns: 56 + 27
Add in columns: 61 + 28
quiz.mistake: Swaps the tens and ones in the answer

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I add 47 + 25 in columns?
teach.praise: Super! Ones first, carry the new ten, then add the tens.
teach.nudge: Which column do I add first? What if the ones make more than 9?

learn.hook: Diwali is here! Riya has 24 diyas and Arjun has 13. How many diyas can they light?
points: Add the ones first. Then add the tens.
If the ones make 10 or more, make a new ten.
Carry the new ten to the tens place and add it there.

example.q: Meena has 36 flowers. She gets 27 more. How many flowers now?
steps: Ones: 6 + 7 = 13. That is 1 ten and 3 ones.
Write 3 in the ones. Carry 1 ten.

learn.reallife: We add when we count sweets in two boxes or runs made in two overs.

quiz.q: Riya has 24 diyas. Arjun has 13 diyas. How many diyas in all?
What is 52 + 30?
quiz.explain: 30 is 3 tens. 5 tens and 3 tens make 8 tens. The 2 ones stay. So 82.
quiz.mistake: Adds the 3 to the ones instead of the tens

quiz.q: Kabir has 36 balloons. He buys 27 more. How many balloons now?
quiz.explain: Ones: 6 + 7 = 13. Write 3 and carry 1 ten. Tens: 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. So 63.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry the new ten

quiz.q: What is 45 + 8?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry, or writes 13 in the ones place

quiz.q: Fill the gap: 40 + ___ = 70
quiz.explain: From 40, count on by 10s: 50, 60, 70. That is 3 tens, or 30.
quiz.mistake: Writes 3 instead of 3 tens, or adds 40 and 70

quiz.q: Which sum is equal to 50?
quiz.mistake: Picks a sum that has 50 in it without adding

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I add 24 and 13?
teach.praise: Super! Add the ones first, then the tens. 24 + 13 = 37!
teach.nudge: Which do I add first, the ones or the tens?

learn.hook: Your piggy bank had 45 coins. Nani gave you 30 more. Now how many?
points: Words like 'more', 'gets', 'buys' and 'gets on' tell us to add.
Start with what we have and add what we get.
Sometimes the total goes past 100: 43 + 58 = 101.
10 tens make 100. More than 10 tens is more than 100.

example.q: A bus has 37 people. 25 more get on. How many people now?

learn.reallife: Cricket scores: 43 runs in one match and 58 in the next make 101!

games.title: True or false?
items: 'Gets more' tells us to take away
Getting more means adding.
6 tens and 5 tens make 11 tens, which is 110.
Adding two 2-digit numbers can never go past 100
30 people on a bus and 12 more get on: now there are 42

quiz.q: Ankit scored 43 runs in one match and 58 in the next. How many runs in all?
Priya had 26 pencils. She bought 15 more. How many pencils now?
Raj has 48 marbles. He wins 36 more. How many marbles now?
A bus has 52 people. 29 more get on. How many people are on the bus now?
quiz.mistake: Takes away because people are moving

quiz.q: Mummy spent ₹65 on fruit and ₹40 on milk. How much did she spend in all?
quiz.explain: 6 tens and 4 tens make 10 tens = 100. Then 5 more: 105.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the total cannot go past 100

quiz.q: Which sum is more than 100?
quiz.mistake: Does not work out each sum

teach.ask: Gappu: Can two 2-digit numbers add up to more than 100?
teach.praise: Yes! Like 43 + 58 = 101. 10 tens make a hundred.
teach.nudge: What if the tens add up to 10 or more?

learn.hook: Is it a 'put together' story or a 'take away' story? Find the clue word!
points: Read the story. Find the numbers.
Words like 'in all' and 'altogether' tell us to add.
Words like 'left', 'gave away' and 'ate' tell us to take away.
'How many more' means find the difference. Take the small number from the big one.
Check: does the answer make sense?

example.q: There are 48 marigold flowers. Meena uses 23 for a garland. How many are left?

learn.reallife: At the market, at a party or in a cricket match, we solve stories like these.

games.title: Add or take away?
items: Riya has 12 diyas and buys 5 more. How many in all?
There were 20 balloons. 6 burst. How many are left?
Arjun ate 3 of his 10 laddoos. How many are left?
8 boys and 9 girls play. How many children altogether?
Kabir gave away 7 of his 15 cards. How many are left?
A train has 30 people. 10 more get on. How many now?

quiz.q: A rangoli has 25 red dots and 32 yellow dots. How many dots in all?
quiz.explain: 'In all' means add. Ones: 5 + 2 = 7. Tens: 2 + 3 = 5. So 57.

quiz.q: There were 40 sweets in a box. The guests ate 18. How many sweets are left?
quiz.explain: 'Left' means take away. 0 is too small to take 8, so break a ten: 10 − 8 = 2. Tens: 3 − 1 = 2. So 22.
quiz.mistake: Does 8 − 0 in the ones instead of breaking a ten

quiz.q: Joseph's team scored 46 runs. The other team scored 38. How many more runs did Joseph's team score?
quiz.explain: 'How many more' means take the small number from the big one. 46 − 38 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Adds the scores, or does 8 − 6 in the ones

quiz.q: A train has 54 people. At a station, 21 get off. How many are on the train now?
quiz.explain: People got off, so take away. Ones: 4 − 1 = 3. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. So 33.
quiz.mistake: Adds the people who got off

quiz.q: Aisha buys a pencil for ₹15 and an eraser for ₹7. How much does she pay?
quiz.explain: She pays for both, so add. ₹15 + ₹5 = ₹20. Then 2 more makes ₹22.
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding, or forgets to carry

quiz.q: Which word in a story tells you to take away?
quiz.explain: 'Left' asks what remains after some are gone. So we take away.

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I know if a story needs adding or taking away?
teach.praise: Clever! 'In all' means add and 'left' means take away. I will look for clue words!
teach.nudge: Which clue words tell me to add? Which words tell me to take away?

topics.title: Taking away on a ginladi and a number line

learn.hook: 10 diyas glow on the wall. The wind blows out 3. How many still glow?
points: Taking away means finding what is left.
On a ginladi, move beads for the first number, then push some back. Count what stays.
On a number line, start at the big number and jump backward.
Jump back in tens first, then in ones: 57 - 23 goes 57, 47, 37, then 36, 35, 34.
learn.reallife: When guests eat sweets from a box, we take away to see how many are left.

games.title: Jumps back for 57 - 23
games.prompt: Put the landing numbers in order for 57 - 23

quiz.q: There are 10 diyas. The wind blows out 3. How many still glow?
On a ginladi, Hari moves 25 beads. He pushes 5 back. How many are left?
Start at 50 on a number line. Jump back 10. Where do you land?
quiz.explain: A jump back of 10 takes away 1 ten. 50 - 10 = 40.

quiz.q: Find 57 - 23 by jumping back 10, 10 and then 3. Where do you land?
Jumps go back from 46 to 36, then to 33. Which subtraction is it?
quiz.explain: 46 to 36 is 10 back. 36 to 33 is 3 back. 10 + 3 = 13.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one of the jumps

quiz.q: Taking away means ___.
quiz.explain: When we take away, we find what is left.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up taking away and adding

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I find 57 - 23 on a number line?
teach.praise: Yes! Start at 57 and jump back 2 tens and 3 ones to reach 34.
teach.nudge: Do I jump forward or back? By how much?

topics.title: Subtracting with blocks and in columns

learn.hook: Take away rods and cubes. What is left is the answer!
points: Show the big number with rods and cubes.
Take cubes from cubes and rods from rods: 37 - 24 leaves 1 rod and 3 cubes, which is 13.
Write numbers in columns: tens under tens, ones under ones.
Subtract the ones first. If the top ones are too few, break 1 ten into 10 ones.

steps: Ones: 2 is less than 8. Break 1 ten: 12 - 8 = 4.

learn.reallife: A shopkeeper checks how many packets are left on the shelf.

quiz.q: Show 37 with blocks. Take away 2 rods and 4 cubes. What is left?
quiz.explain: Rods: 3 - 2 = 1. Cubes: 7 - 4 = 3. 1 rod and 3 cubes is 13.
quiz.mistake: Adds the blocks instead of taking away

quiz.q: Subtract in columns: 68 - 25
In 52 - 17, the ones are 2 - 7. What do we do first?
quiz.explain: 2 is less than 7, so break 1 ten. Now the ones are 12, and 12 - 7 = 5.
quiz.mistake: Takes the small digit from the big one

quiz.q: Subtract in columns: 52 - 17
Subtract in columns: 70 - 26
Subtract in columns: 93 - 41

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I do 52 - 17? 2 is smaller than 7!
teach.praise: Yes! Break 1 ten into 10 ones. 12 - 7 = 5, and 4 - 1 = 3. Answer 35!
teach.nudge: What can I do when the top ones are too few?

learn.hook: Harpreet made 45 laddoos. Her friends ate 12. How many are left?
points: Take away the ones first. Then take away the tens.
If the top ones digit is too small, break 1 ten into 10 ones.
Check by adding: 33 + 12 = 45.

example.q: Joseph has 52 marbles. He gives away 27. How many are left?
steps: Break 1 ten. Now there are 4 tens and 12 ones.

learn.reallife: We take away to find how many sweets are left or how much money we get back.

games.title: True or false?
items: 5 tens take away 2 tens leaves 3 tens.
64 comes from adding. 43 − 21 = 22.
Adding back the part we took away gives the first number.
In 52 − 27, we can just do 7 − 2 in the ones.
We must take 7 from 2. 2 is too small, so we break a ten first.
1 less than 80 is 79.

quiz.q: Harpreet made 45 laddoos. Her friends ate 12. How many laddoos are left?
What is 80 − 30?
quiz.explain: 8 tens take away 3 tens leaves 5 tens. 5 tens is 50.
quiz.mistake: Adds the numbers, or forgets the 0 in the ones

quiz.q: What is 52 − 27?
quiz.explain: 2 is too small to take 7. Break a ten: 12 − 7 = 5. Then 4 tens − 2 tens = 2 tens. So 25.
quiz.mistake: Takes the smaller ones digit from the bigger one (7 − 2) instead of breaking a ten

quiz.q: Aisha had 30 bangles. She gave 8 to her sister. How many does Aisha have now?
quiz.explain: Count back 8 from 30: 29, 28, 27, 26, 25, 24, 23, 22. So 22 are left.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of taking away, or counts 30 itself while counting back

quiz.q: Fill the gap: 90 − ___ = 50
quiz.explain: From 90 go back by 10s to 50: 80, 70, 60, 50. That is 4 tens, or 40.
quiz.mistake: Writes 4 instead of 4 tens, or adds the numbers

quiz.q: Kabir has 61 stickers. He uses 25. How many stickers are left?
quiz.explain: 1 is too small to take 5. Break a ten: 11 − 5 = 6. Then 5 tens − 2 tens = 3 tens. So 36.
quiz.mistake: Does 5 − 1 in the ones, or forgets that one ten was broken

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I take 12 away from 45?
teach.praise: Yes! Take away the ones, then the tens. 45 − 12 = 33!
teach.nudge: What do I take away first, the ones or the tens?

learn.hook: Dadi gave you ₹82. You bought a kite for ₹22. How much is left?
points: Money left = money we had - money we spent.
Flowers left = flowers we had - flowers given away.
If we buy two things, add their costs first, then take that away from our money.
Check: money left + money spent = money we had.

example.q: Ria had ₹78. She spent ₹61 on gifts. How much is left?

learn.reallife: At the mela, children check how much pocket money is left after each ride.

games.title: True or false?
items: You had ₹40 and spent ₹25, so ₹25 is left
To find money left, we take away what we spent
Spending makes our money less.
Spending ₹24 and ₹37 means spending ₹61
Giving away flowers makes our flowers more
Giving away makes them fewer.

quiz.q: Arun had ₹82. He bought a kite for ₹22. How much money is left?
Lata had ₹60. She spent ₹20 on a ride. How much is left?
quiz.explain: 6 tens take away 2 tens leaves 4 tens. ₹40.

quiz.q: Mira had 28 flowers. She gave 5 to her friend. How many are left?
A garland maker had 73 flowers. He gave 47 to the temple. How many are left?
Neel had ₹78. He spent ₹24 on a book and ₹37 on colours. How much is left?
quiz.mistake: Takes away only one of the costs

quiz.q: Sita had ₹50. After buying a toy she has ₹15 left. How much did the toy cost?
quiz.mistake: Adds the money left to the money she had

teach.ask: Gappu: I had ₹82 and spent ₹22. How do I find what is left?
teach.nudge: Should I add or take away what I spent?

learn.hook: Seema wants to skip 20 times. She has done 14. How many more skips?
points: 'How many more to reach' means find the gap.
Count on from the small number to the big number.
Or take away: 20 - 14 = 6.
For a missing number like 56 + ? = 87, find 87 - 56 = 31.

example.q: There are 56 birds on a tree. More come and now there are 87. How many came?

learn.reallife: How many more runs to win the match? Count on from your score!

quiz.q: Seema wants to skip 20 times. She has done 14 skips. How many more?
quiz.explain: Count on from 14 to 20: 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20. That is 6.

quiz.q: There were 56 birds on a tree. More came, and now there are 87. How many birds came?
Tapan has tapped a drum 18 times. He wants 35 taps. How many more taps?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the gap

quiz.q: Fill the missing number: 42 + ___ = 60
A team needs 75 runs to win. They have 48. How many more runs do they need?
Kavi has 30 stickers. He wants 45. Which tells how many more he needs?
quiz.explain: The gap from 30 to 45 is found by 45 - 30 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds when looking for a gap

teach.ask: Gappu: I have done 14 skips. I want 20. How many more?
teach.praise: Yes! Count on from 14 to 20, or do 20 - 14. It is 6.
teach.nudge: Can I count on from 14? How far to 20?

learn.hook: One addition fact hides two subtraction facts! Let us find them.
points: These facts belong to one fact family.
Changing the order in addition does not change the sum: 25 + 14 = 14 + 25 = 39.
Use a fact family to fill a missing number.
learn.reallife: 12 boys and 8 girls make 20 children. So 20 - 8 tells us the number of boys.

games.title: True or false?
items: Changing the order does not change the sum.
Take away one part to get the other part.
43 - 21 and 21 - 43 give the same answer
In taking away the order matters. 43 - 21 = 22.
9 + 6 = 15 is in the fact family of 6, 9 and 15
6 + 9, 9 + 6, 15 - 6 and 15 - 9 are all in it.

quiz.q: 30 + 20 = 50. Which subtraction fact is in the same family?
quiz.explain: Take away one part, 20, from the whole, 50, to get the other part, 30.
quiz.mistake: Uses numbers not in the family

quiz.explain: Changing the order does not change the sum. It is still 39.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the order changes the answer

quiz.q: Fill the fact family: 47 + 22 = 69, so 69 - 22 = ___
quiz.explain: Take away one part from the whole to get the other part: 47.

quiz.q: Fill the gap: 36 + ___ = 58
Which shows that changing the order does not change the sum?
quiz.mistake: Thinks order does not matter in taking away too

quiz.q: 40, 15 and 55 make a fact family. Which fact is NOT in it?
quiz.explain: 25 is not one of the numbers 40, 15, 55. The other three facts use only these numbers.
quiz.mistake: Does not check which numbers belong

teach.ask: Gappu: 30 + 20 = 50. What subtraction facts can I make from this?
teach.nudge: What do I get if I take 20 away from 50? And 30?

learn.hook: Build a number pyramid! Each block is the sum of the two blocks under it.
points: In a number pyramid, add the two blocks below to get the block above.
Blocks 12 and 15 below make 27 above.
If the top block and one block below are known, take away: top 40, one block 25, the other is 15.
The same rule works in other add-the-two-below diagrams.

example.q: Bottom row: 10, 14, 6. Find the middle row and the top.

learn.reallife: Fruit sellers stack oranges in a pyramid. Each orange rests on two below!

quiz.q: In a pyramid, the two blocks below are 12 and 15. What is in the block above?
In a pyramid, the top block is 40. One block below is 25. What is the other block below?
quiz.mistake: Adds the top and the block below

quiz.q: The bottom row of a pyramid is 10, 14, 6. What are the two middle blocks?
quiz.mistake: Takes away the blocks instead of adding

quiz.q: Bottom row 10, 14, 6 gives a middle row of 24 and 20. What is the top block?
Two blocks below are 35 and ___. The block above is 62. What is missing?
Bottom row 5, 8, 7. Middle row 13 and 15. What is the top block?

teach.ask: Gappu: How do I fill the block above 12 and 15 in a pyramid?
teach.praise: Yes! Add the two blocks below: 12 + 15 = 27.
teach.nudge: What do I do with the two blocks under it?

learn.hook: Some sums on the board are wrong! Be the checker.
points: Check an addition by doing it again carefully, ones first.
A common mistake is forgetting to carry: 38 + 25 is 63, not 53.
Another mistake is taking the small ones digit from the big one: 52 - 17 is 35, not 45.
Check a subtraction by adding: 35 + 17 = 52.
learn.reallife: Shopkeepers check bills twice so no one pays the wrong amount.

games.title: True or false?
items: We can add 35 + 17 to check 52 - 17 = 35
35 + 17 = 52, so the subtraction is right.
In 52 - 17 we can just do 7 - 2 in the ones
We must break a ten: 12 - 7 = 5.

quiz.q: Raju wrote 46 + 37 = 73. What is the right answer?
quiz.explain: Ones: 6 + 7 = 13, write 3 and carry 1. Tens: 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. So 83.

quiz.q: What mistake did Raju make in 46 + 37 = 73?
options: He took away instead of adding
quiz.explain: The ones made 13. He wrote 3 but did not carry the 1 ten.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the missing carry

quiz.q: Sana wrote 52 - 17 = 45. What is the right answer?
Which mistake gives 52 - 17 = 45?
options: Doing 7 - 2 instead of breaking a ten
quiz.explain: Doing 7 - 2 skips breaking a ten, so the tens stay 5 - 1 = 4. That gives 45. The right way: 12 - 7 = 5 and 4 - 1 = 3, so 35.
quiz.mistake: Does not know when to break a ten

quiz.q: Which sum is correct?
Ishan says 90 - 34 = 66. What is the right answer?
quiz.mistake: Forgets that one ten was broken

teach.ask: Gappu: I wrote 46 + 37 = 73. Is it right?
teach.praise: Good checking! I forgot to carry. It is 83.
teach.nudge: What do the ones add up to? Did I carry the ten?
